content:
Order fulfillment for supply chain managers and logistics providers is important for smooth functioning. A lack of items in the inventory at the right time can delay the shipments and incur losses for the business. Such a situation affects logistics and supply chain businesses and others that depend on the product shipment.

So, why is inventory visibility vital for supply chains?

Inventory visibility refers to the understanding or visibility of products in stock in a company or supply chain warehouse. It includes item details like product name, batch, manufacturing details, number of products, rack locations, order details, and much more. It allows business organizations to plan out the ordering requirements. Inventory visibility helps them keep track of raw materials and products that they want.

For supply chains, inventory visibility offers many benefits, including the following:

  • Increase efficiency
  • Maintain inventory levels
  • Demand forecasting
  • Improve customer experience
  • Improved ROI

Let’s explore the benefits of inventory visibility more.

Increase Efficiency

Gaining the overall visibility for all the inventory items gives you an idea of what is where in stocks. Historic and current inventory data can leverage the internal processes and boost the supply chain processes. Inventory data can help supply chains to analyze multiple points and figure out possible errors in the system.

Maintain Inventory Levels

With adequate visibility, supply chain managers can maintain inventory levels of the various products or raw materials in the warehouses. Based on demands, they can maintain sufficiently extra items as and when the levels go down. Intelligent supply chain management platforms can help the business to maintain and order in such conditions.

Forecast Demands

Inventory visibility gives access to historical data of who ordered what and when from the warehouses. It can also determine the number of orders that go out to each customer. Based on this data, tech-enabled applications can forecast demand requirements for each item in the inventory. This helps the supply chain businesses to be ready when the demand comes in.

Improve Customer Experience

Customers prefer to get their orders without delay and on time. With proper inventory visibility, supply chains can ensure that they satisfy this condition without error. With data and inventory management systems, supply chain managers can optimize stock levels, save logistics costs, and reduce last-mile delivery issues.

Improved ROI

For supply chain businesses, having a product sitting in the warehouse occupying space is a loss of investment. As it represents tied-up cash, it is imperative to avoid such situations. With proper visibility, supply chains can avoid such situations and keep only the products that can go soon without wasting space longer. This method can help them improve ROI.

Supply chain businesses can overcome multiple challenges with inventory visibility. Let us know what your challenges was.

title: How AI is Transforming the Insurance Industry
excerpt: The insurance industry is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI). From streamlining claims processing to enhancing customer experiences, AI is reshaping traditional insurance practices and paving the way for innovative solutions.   This blog explores how AI is revolutionizing the insurance sector and the benefits it brings to insurers and […]
content:
The insurance industry is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI). From streamlining claims processing to enhancing customer experiences, AI is reshaping traditional insurance practices and paving the way for innovative solutions.  

This blog explores how AI is revolutionizing the insurance sector and the benefits it brings to insurers and policyholders alike. 

Enhancing Claims Processing 

One of the most notable impacts of AI in the insurance industry is its ability to streamline claims processing. Traditional claims processing can be time-consuming and prone to errors. AI-driven systems, however, can quickly analyze vast amounts of data, identify patterns, and automate the entire process. This reduces the time required to settle claims and minimizes the risk of human error. 

AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can handle initial claims inquiries, guide policyholders through the process, and even assess damage using image recognition technology. This not only speeds up the claims process but also enhances customer satisfaction by providing quick and accurate responses. 

Improving Risk Assessment 

Accurate risk assessment is crucial for determining insurance premiums and coverage. AI technologies, such as machine learning algorithms, can analyze historical data and identify risk factors more precisely than traditional methods. This enables insurers to create more accurate risk profiles and offer personalized policies that reflect the actual risk associated with an individual or entity. 

AI can also monitor real-time data from various sources, such as social media, IoT devices, and telematics, to continuously update risk assessments. This proactive approach helps insurers to adjust premiums dynamically and prevent potential losses before they occur. 

Enhancing Customer Experiences 

AI is transforming customer interactions in the insurance industry by providing personalized and efficient services. Chatbots and virtual assistants can handle routine inquiries, offer policy recommendations, and assist with claims, freeing up human agents to focus on more complex tasks. These AI-driven tools are available 24/7, ensuring that customers receive support whenever they need it. 

Furthermore, AI can analyze customer data to gain insights into their preferences and behaviors. This enables insurers to offer tailored products and services that meet individual needs, enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty. 

Fraud Detection and Prevention 

Insurance fraud is a significant issue that costs the industry billions of dollars each year. AI can help combat fraud by analyzing data to detect suspicious patterns and anomalies. Machine learning algorithms can flag potentially fraudulent claims for further investigation, reducing the time and resources spent on manual reviews. 

AI can also monitor transactions in real-time, identifying fraudulent activities as they occur. This proactive approach not only helps prevent fraud but also protects legitimate policyholders from bearing the financial burden of fraudulent claims. 

Revolutionizing Underwriting 

AI is revolutionizing the underwriting process by enabling more accurate and efficient evaluations. Traditional underwriting often relies on limited data and manual processes, leading to inconsistent results. AI algorithms, on the other hand, can analyze vast amounts of data from multiple sources, providing underwriters with deeper insights into potential risks. 

This enhanced analytical capability allows for more precise pricing and policy customization. As a result, insurers can offer more competitive rates while maintaining profitability. 

Conclusion 

Artificial intelligence is transforming the insurance industry by enhancing claims processing, improving risk assessment, elevating customer experiences, detecting fraud, and revolutionizing underwriting. These advancements not only improve operational efficiency but also provide significant benefits to policyholders through faster service, personalized policies, and increased security.

As AI continues to evolve, its impact on the insurance industry will undoubtedly grow, driving further innovation and improvement.

In today’s digital era, financial transactions have become more convenient than ever before, with online banking, mobile payments, and e-commerce dominating the landscape.  

However, this convenience also brings about increased risks of cyber threats and fraud. Safeguarding your financial transactions is paramount to protect your assets and personal information from unauthorized access.  

In this blog, we’ll explore essential strategies and tools to navigate the digital frontier and ensure the security of your financial transactions. 

Understanding the Risks

In today’s interconnected world, staying informed about the evolving landscape of cyber threats is crucial to protect your financial well-being. 

Cyber Threats 

Malicious actors constantly target financial institutions and individuals through various cyber-attacks, including phishing scams, malware, and identity theft. 

Data Breaches 

Breaches in cybersecurity can lead to the exposure of sensitive financial data, putting individuals at risk of financial fraud and identity theft. 

Fraudulent Activities 

With the proliferation of online transactions, fraudsters exploit vulnerabilities to conduct fraudulent activities such as unauthorized transactions and account takeovers. 

Key Strategies for Safeguarding Financial Transactions

By proactively implementing these key strategies, you can fortify your defenses and minimize the risk of falling victim to financial fraud or cyber-attacks. 

Strong Authentication 

Utilize multi-factor authentication (MFA) methods, such as one-time passwords or biometric authentication, to add an extra layer of security to your online accounts. 

Secure Networks 

Ensure that you access online banking and make transactions only through secure and trusted networks, such as encrypted Wi-Fi connections or virtual private networks (VPNs). 

Regular Monitoring 

Keep a close eye on your financial accounts for any suspicious activities or unauthorized transactions. Promptly report any discrepancies to your financial institution. 

Update Software 

Keep your devices and software up to date with the latest security patches and updates to protect against known vulnerabilities. 

Educate Yourself 

Stay informed about common fraud schemes and cybersecurity best practices to recognize and avoid potential threats effectively. 

Tools for Enhanced Financial Transaction Security

By leveraging these advanced tools and technologies, you can significantly enhance the security of your financial transactions and safeguard your assets against cyber threats. 

Encryption 

Encrypt sensitive financial data during transmission and storage to prevent unauthorized access and protect against data breaches. 

Fraud Detection Systems

Many financial institutions employ advanced fraud detection systems that analyze transaction patterns and detect suspicious activities in real-time. 

Virtual Cards 

Consider using virtual credit cards for online purchases, which provide temporary card numbers and enhanced security features to minimize the risk of fraud. 

Security Apps 

Explore security apps and tools designed to enhance the security of your financial transactions, such as password managers, antivirus software, and identity theft protection services. 

Conclusion

Safeguarding your financial transactions is crucial in today’s digital age, where cyber threats are prevalent and evolving. By implementing robust security strategies and leveraging the right tools, you can navigate the digital frontier with confidence and protect your financial assets effectively.

Stay vigilant, stay informed, and take proactive steps to ensure the security of your financial transactions in an increasingly interconnected world.

title: How Smart AI Checkouts Help Retailers
excerpt: Computer vision AI systems have the ability to reliably identify objects in digital image forms. AI developers are using this capability across a range of industries to improve efficiency, customer experience, and security. Object detection can be of particular value in retail. Retailers are starting to introduce AI into their stores in the form of […]
content:
Computer vision AI systems have the ability to reliably identify objects in digital image forms. AI developers are using this capability across a range of industries to improve efficiency, customer experience, and security. Object detection can be of particular value in retail. Retailers are starting to introduce AI into their stores in the form of Smart AI Checkout. These devices can help retail workers in many ways. 

However, for AI checkouts to reach their full potential, AI developers need to train them with accurately annotated image data. Annotating data in-house can be a distracting challenge for AI companies, which is why many developers choose to partner with annotation services. 

How AI Checkout Works 

Smart checkouts work by identifying any object that moves into a camera’s field of view, which is located above the scanning device. Therefore, the AI system can identify the object and match it with the scanned barcode, giving the checkout more information than is available in a normal barcode-only situation. Retailers can use this information in multiple ways as listed below. 

  • Gain more information 
  • Detect suspicious transactions 
  • Accelerate checkouts 
  • Monitor thefts 
  • Determine patterns 

Gain more information 

Smart AI checkouts can collect a huge amount of data about shopping habits. AI models use data collected by computer vision systems to create detailed reports and suggestions for retail managers. 

Detect Suspicious Transactions 

The main function of smart registers is to prevent theft. If the item in the camera view does not match the scanned barcode, this may mean that an item exchange is taking place. In addition, the system can indicate when customers fail to scan items. Smart checkouts can send alerts to store security when potential theft is detected. 

Accelerate Checkouts 

Smart checkouts can make self-scanning easier. When customers try to register items without barcodes (usually fruit and vegetables), smart registers can offer them a pick list of options, which is easier than scrolling through a list of all items. 

Monitor Theft 

The presence of eye-level cameras at checkouts can act as a deterrent to theft. When shoplifters know a transaction is being recorded, they typically do not risk stealing items. 

Determine Patterns 

Smart POS systems are good at recognizing patterns. This allows them to identify which items are most frequently stolen or which products are the most difficult to scan. It helps the retailer prevent product loss and improve customer experience. 

How AI Checkout Is Implemented 

Implementing the AI checkout system is much easier than we think it is for retailers. It can be summarized into four stages or steps. 

  • Session start 
  • Shopper detection 
  • Product detection 
  • checkout 

Session Start 

Stores can use turnstiles to initiate shopping by scanning a QR code. At this point, the system matches the profile and digital wallet with the actual person entering the store. 

Shopper Detection 

This is the detection and tracking of people and objects that are done via computer vision cameras. Cameras simply remember who the person is, and as soon as they pick a product off the shelf, the system places it in a virtual shopping cart. Some stores use hundreds of cameras to see from different angles and cover all store zones. 

Product Detection 

As soon as the person picks something off the shelf and takes it with them, cameras capture that action. When the product image on the video is matched to the actual product in the retailer database, the store places an item in a virtual shopping cart. 

Checkout 

When the product list is ready, the person can just walk out. When the person leaves a zone captured by cameras, computer vision considers this to be the end of a shopping session. This causes the system to calculate the total amount and debit the customer’s digital wallet.

content:
Artificial Intelligence is among the most valuable tools we have today. From disease detection and drug discovery to climate change models, AI is continually offering insights and solutions that are helping us address the most pressing challenges of our time.

In financial services, one of the main problems we are faced with is inequality when it comes to financial inclusion. Though this inequality is driven by many factors, the common denominator in each case is likely to be data.

Data Is Crucial to Businesses

In financial services, one of the main problems we are faced with is inequality when it comes to financial inclusion. Though this inequality is driven by many factors, the common denominator in each case is likely to be data. Data is the lifeblood of most organizations, but especially so for organizations seeking to implement advanced automation through AI and machine learning.

Hence, financial services organizations and the data science community must understand how models can be used to create a more inclusive financial services landscape.

Lending Drives Revenues

Lending is an essential financial service today. It drives revenue for banks and loan providers, but also provides a core service for both individuals and businesses.

But in each case, loan risk must be evaluated.

The majority of loan default risk today is calculated via automated tools. Increasingly, this automation is provided by algorithms that greatly expedite the decision-making process.

Loan providers must consider the more nuanced factors behind making “the right decision”. With the demand for loans booming, particularly as point-of-sale loans such as buy-now-pay-later offer new and flexible ways to gain credit, there is now a wealth of competition in the industry, with traditional lenders, challengers and Fintechs all vying for market share.

Build a Culture of Fairness

When a loan risk model rejects applications, it’s possible that many of the unsuccessful applicants will implicitly understand the logic behind the decision. They may have applied knowing that they would not likely meet the acceptance criteria, or simply miscalculated their eligibility.

But what happens when a member of a minority group or individual is rejected, based on the fact that they fall outside the majority group on which a model was trained?

If a small business owner has the means to pay back their loan, but is rejected for no discernible reason, they will quite rightly be upset at their mistreatment and may seek a competitor to provide the services they require.

The data science and financial services communities should elevate equitable outcomes for all. We must seek to prioritize people in addition to model performance.

Eliminate Bias

Despite regulations that rightly prevent the use of sensitive information for use in decision-making algorithms, unfairness can creep in through the use of biased data.

Here are five examples of how data bias can occur:

  • Missing data
  • Sample bias
  • Exclusion bias
  • Measurement bias
  • Label bias

Simply understanding how bias can find its way into models is a good start when it comes to bringing about a more inclusive financial services environment.

title: Transform into a Circular Economy with These 5 Steps
excerpt: From metals, minerals, and fossil fuels to organic materials, 100 billion tons of natural resources enter the market annually. content:
From metals, minerals, and fossil fuels to organic materials, 100 billion tons of natural resources enter the market annually. This rampant consumption has devastating effects on people, wildlife, and the planet. It is more important than ever to move from linear, use-and-throw models to a circular economy; where waste and pollution are planned, products and materials last longer.

However, circular economy is not just about fixing environmental issues. It brings great opportunities and positive impacts across industries, sectors, and the life of people. A growing number of businesses, governments, and civil society organizations are coming together to drive change in this approach.

More than 200 experts from 100 organizations helped develop a set of action plans, that analyze potential impacts and calls for action in five key sectors: plastics, textiles, electronics, food, and capital equipment.

The action plan presents five options in relation to the transition to a circular economy, which are as follows

  • Better usage of finite resources
  • Reduce emissions
  • Protect health and biodiversity
  • Boost economy
  • Create jobs

What if we could build an economy that uses things instead of consuming them? Circular economy prefers actions that preserve value. This means sustainable design, reuse, reproduction, and recycling to keep products, components and materials moving through the economy. Circular systems make efficient use of bio-based materials, encouraging them to be used in many different ways as they move between the economy and natural systems.

Reduce Emissions

The carbon dioxide emissions of a circular economy are lower than those of a linear economy. The production of new materials leads to the release of carbon dioxide; the circular economy minimizes the need to produce new materials by maximizing resource recovery and thus eliminates the carbon costs associated with producing new materials.

In other words, the circular economy tries to plan for waste, and the emission of carbon dioxide is almost always waste. According to the 2021 Circularity Gap report, the circular economy could reduce global greenhouse gases by 39 percent. To reduce emissions, companies and governments must first  measure them. The entire value chain must be considered. By analyzing  the location of emissions and identifying cycles such as production, transport and material use, the circular economy can act as a catalyst to achieve emission reductions.

Boost Economy

The widespread adoption of the circular economy will lead to an increase in the gross domestic product (GDP) – by 2030. But it’s not just a general financial boost. Individual companies practicing the circular economy can also receive financial benefits.

The ability to reuse materials in the manufacture of new products instead of purchasing new materials can reduce operating costs in the long run. Reuse of existing materials also removes the industry’s dependence on resources that are otherwise volatile, either in price or availability. If the circular economy promotes sustainable innovation and production processes, jobs are needed to sustain them. The growth potential of this industry – both in terms of capital and jobs – can only grow.

Around one in four American adults are underbanked, meaning they are underserved by traditional finance and rely on high-fee alternative financial systems. Underbanked Americans find it almost impossible to get a loan or a credit card.

For those who do have a credit score, it’s often not a very high one. As a result, these Americans turn to money orders, payday lenders, and check cashing services.

Underbanked Americans are much less capable of ‘getting ahead’ financially, which further perpetuates the cycle of poverty. To prosper, every American person needs equitable access to traditional financial services.

Traditional Credit Scores are Outdated

Traditional credit scores are outdated and often irrelevant in today’s economy. They fail to account for data like employment history and financial behavior, which are important factors in predicting credit risk.

Let us explore how Artificial Intelligence could make your credit score obsolete.

AI is Enabling Better Credit Systems and Early Wage Access

AI can help lenders assess a borrower’s risk more accurately. It can do this by analyzing data that is not included in a traditional credit score, like whether the borrower spends their capital on necessities or luxuries. AI could also help lenders identify potential risk factors that may not be obvious, like whether a borrower is using too much of their available credit.

Replacing Traditional Credit Scores

in the future, AI may be able to replace traditional credit scores altogether. This would allow more Americans, including those who are unbanked, to gain access to traditional financial services. This would also help to reduce the risk of default for lenders, which would lead to lower interest rates and fewer fees.

The traditional credit scoring model is a global problem. In Africa, for example, around 57% of the population is “credit invisible” — meaning they do not have a bank account or credit score.

Empowering the Underserved

AI-based solutions are empowering the underserved by giving them access to traditional financial services. This, in turn, is helping to break the cycle of poverty and improve their ability to get ahead financially.

One analysis found that providing access to traditional financial services increased the presence of businesses in the area by 7.6% while driving higher income levels. Traditional financial services allow people to save money, invest in their businesses, and make purchases that they couldn’t otherwise make.

AI is making it easier for lenders to assess a borrower’s risk. This is helping to empower the underserved by giving them access to traditional financial services.

Financial Inclusion Increases Economic Growth

Financial inclusion can even increase economic growth. A study by the International Monetary Fund found that, for a country with a low level of financial inclusion, improving financial inclusion to the 75th percentile would lead to a 2% to 3% increase in GDP growth.

Something to Ponder

While AI won’t replace credit scores overnight, it is clear that it has the potential to do so in the future. This would be a game-changing development, as it would give up to 1.7 billion people around the world access to traditional financial services.

In the ever-evolving landscape of the internet, the transition from Web 2.0 to Web 3.0 marks a significant paradigm shift, offering businesses new opportunities and challenges alike. As we embark on this digital journey, understanding the differences between Web 3.0 and its predecessor is crucial for determining the best approach for your business in 2024. Let’s explore the nuances of Web 3.0 versus Web 2.0 and their implications for businesses seeking to thrive in the digital age.

Defining Web 2.0: The Era of Interactivity

Web 2.0, characterized by user-generated content, social media platforms, and interactive web applications, revolutionized the way people engage with the internet. From the rise of social networking sites like Facebook and Twitter to the proliferation of blogging platforms and multimedia-sharing platforms like YouTube, Web 2.0 democratized content creation and consumption, fostering a culture of collaboration and connectivity.

Introducing Web 3.0: The Era of Decentralization and Interoperability

Web 3.0 represents the next evolutionary stage of the Internet, driven by emerging technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Unlike its predecessor, Web 3.0 aims to decentralize control, enhance data privacy, and enable seamless interoperability across disparate platforms and systems. This decentralized approach promises to empower users with greater autonomy over their digital identities and assets while fostering trust and transparency in online interactions.

Enhanced Security and Data Privacy

One of the key advantages of Web 3.0 is its emphasis on enhanced security and data privacy. By leveraging blockchain technology and cryptographic protocols, Web 3.0 platforms offer robust protection against cyber threats and unauthorized access. Moreover, users have greater control over their data, with the ability to securely manage and monetize their digital assets. This heightened focus on security and privacy is particularly appealing to businesses operating in sectors where data protection is paramount, such as finance, healthcare, and e-commerce.

Opportunities for Decentralized Finance (DeFi) and Tokenization

Web 3.0 paves the way for the proliferation of decentralized finance (DeFi) applications and tokenization platforms, offering innovative solutions for fundraising, asset management, and peer-to-peer transactions. By leveraging blockchain technology, businesses can tokenize assets, create digital currencies, and participate in decentralized lending and borrowing protocols. This opens up new avenues for fundraising, investment, and financial inclusion, revolutionizing traditional finance models and empowering individuals and businesses alike.

Challenges and Considerations

While Web 3.0 holds immense promise, it also presents unique challenges and considerations for businesses. Transitioning to decentralized platforms may require significant investment in infrastructure, talent, and regulatory compliance. Moreover, interoperability issues and standardization efforts are still evolving, posing challenges for seamless integration across diverse ecosystems. Businesses must carefully weigh the potential benefits and risks of embracing Web 3.0 and develop strategic roadmaps to navigate this digital frontier effectively.

In conclusion, the transition from Web 2.0 to Web 3.0 heralds a new era of decentralization, interoperability, and digital innovation. While Web 3.0 offers compelling opportunities for enhanced security, data privacy, and decentralized finance, businesses must carefully evaluate their readiness and strategic objectives before embracing this paradigm shift. By understanding the nuances of Web 3.0 versus Web 2.0, businesses can chart a course toward digital transformation and position themselves for success in 2024 and beyond.

title: Wireless Network Bridges and WAPs
excerpt: The world is moving towards digital transformation. And digital needs wireless. The bigger the facility the harder this task can get. For example, a factory with an automation assembly plant, manufacturing complex, or other large industrial facilities. System integrators and network administrators face several challenges to ensure high performance, low latency, reliable, secure, and scalable […]
content:
The world is moving towards digital transformation. And digital needs wireless. The bigger the facility the harder this task can get. For example, a factory with an automation assembly plant, manufacturing complex, or other large industrial facilities.

System integrators and network administrators face several challenges to ensure high performance, low latency, reliable, secure, and scalable connectivity. One of the many decisions they face is the deployment of wireless access points (WAP) or antennas and wireless bridges.

A bridge is often used interchangeably with the access point (AP) or any device that supports network bridging. It can be monitored by universal wireless devices with access point functions and bridge, router, and repeaters as configurable options. Today, the bridge may not be a device so much as an available function.

The Difference

The difference between wireless bridge technology techniques and wireless base station technologies is the ultimate goal. A bridge connects two physically separate networks or network segments with a wireless signal at OSI layer 2 (data layer), enabling node-to-node communication between the source and destination.

On the other hand, WAPs act as portals through which multiple wireless devices—IP cameras, laptops, robots, sensors, automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and sensors—access the Internet or an organization’s local area networks (LANs). The WAP connects to a wired router, industrial switch, internet gateway, or hub using an Ethernet cable and mirrors the wireless signal throughout the office or building. WAPs are used for many things such as increasing the speed, reliability, range of existing wireless networks, etc.

LANs are typically divided into multiple segments to avoid traffic congestion or interference or for cost or other management, control, or security reasons. These segments must be integrated or “bridged” so that traffic can be distributed between them. In effect, a  wireless bridge creates one of two “flat” LAN segments on a network. Any LAN protocol can be bridged, but most LANs today are Ethernet-switched LANs, so most bridges are Ethernet bridges.

ALSO READ: Here Is How Automation Reduce Construction Workload

Go Wireless

In the past, a network administrator could only connect two bridge devices with a long Ethernet cable. Industrial-grade wireless networks now reliably perform the same task without the hassle, installation, maintenance, and ongoing costs of ethernet cables or line lease. Now, the wireless bridge quickly connects segments with antennas that emit radio frequency (RF) signals that can span long distances between buildings and machines on the same campus and send and receive data through walls.

Wireless bridging occurs between two transmitter-receivers, rather than between antennas between a single transmitter that sends a signal to multiple receivers. This is why wireless bridge connections are called point-to-point links. It is clear that a wireless bridge is a much more durable and economical alternative to cable installation, especially in hard-to-reach and dangerous industrial sites.

A wireless bridge is more convenient for scaling a network, moving network devices, or connecting clients to other LAN segments. In an industrial environment, using remote Ethernet cables can be impractical or even impossible, leaving a wireless connection as the only option.

The development of any business is not a smooth journey. From market fluctuations to changes in rules and regulations, there are many reasons that challenge a business. Even the infusion of timely funds and investments can’t guarantee the longevity of the business. At times like these, mergers and acquisitions can bring hope to entrepreneurs and business leaders. A business merger enables a company to merge and incorporate different companies under a single banner and expand its horizons.

Business mergers are of different types. Understanding each type of merger can not only expand your business but also improve the quality of your services and products. The merging businesses need to have a clear-cut goal to merge and business goals from the start. It helps the concerned parties to be in a win-win situation, structure the business documents, and perfect the merger agreements. The different types of business mergers help businesses in multiple ways.

Here are five types of business mergers you should know about.

  1. Horizontal merger
  2. Market extension merger
  3. Vertical merger
  4. Product extension merger
  5. Conglomerations

Let’s explore some of them.

Horizontal mergers

Horizontal mergers focus more on market shares with competing companies. The merging companies may have similar products and/or services in the same market space. Instead of competing with each other and losing market share, such businesses can merge to cooperate together and gain complete market control. It helps companies to scale economies, reduce operational costs, increase service quality, and boost quantitative production.

Market extension merger

Each business has its own marketing sphere in the world. If they want to expand their markets to new geographical locations, then they face multiple challenges in this regard. From laws, regulations, competitions, collaboration difficulties, taxes, and much more the challenges are endless. Market extension business merger helps the companies to merge with an existing company in the target market. It helps both parties to extend the market and be more productive in sales.

Vertical merger

The vertical business merger is between companies that are in the same field but not necessarily competitors. This type of merger is seen more in the supply chain and logistics industry where they can share resources and products with each other. This kind of merger depends on the market demands and requirements of raw materials.

Each business can enrich its demands and shortage with each other’s help. It also helps them to add value to their business. For example, a hotel chain merging with agricultural production plant supplying fresh products for business. While the hotels get a continuous supply of raw materials, the agricultural company will gain constant business for their products. content:
After ‘n’ number of alterations, adoptions, and modifications, power over ethernet (PoE) technology is now mature and usable. One of the most used cases of a PoE system is the IP security camera. Organizations with large infrastructures find the usage of IP cameras very beneficial. PoE reduces the need for separate wiring for power cables as previously security cameras needed both internet and power cables. PoE reduces the usage of power cables as it is already combined with PoE cables.

So, how power over ethernet can enhance IP security cameras? Keep reading to know more.

Benefits of Power over Ethernet

PoE system works with less constraint on the IP cameras. It can benefit IP security cameras by providing the following features and capabilities.

  • Flexibility in placement
  • Reduce maintenance
  • Low installation cost
  • Scalability
  • Network reliability

Flexibility in Placement

As PoE security camera systems receive power from the ethernet cable, the organization need not worry about the power cable connection or outlet to each camera. It allows them to be flexible in the camera placement. Changing places, if necessary, will also be easier due to this, as they only have to dismount the camera and the ethernet wire.

Reduce Maintenance

Electric cables and outlets have higher maintenance costs and frequency. Since there is half the wiring to maintain it is easier to maintain the IP camera. IP security cameras are connected to the cloud directly, making error troubleshooting easier. All you have to manage is the camera, ethernet cable, and PoE switches.

Low Installation Costs

Due to the all-purpose nature of PoE cable, you don’t need the presence of certified electricians to remove or maintain the IP security camera. Anybody can do the maintenance, reducing maintenance costs to a great extent.

Scalability

Businesses can increase or decrease the number of IP security cameras as per the need. It only needs the ethernet cables to be wired to the desired location. The installation process is faster and simpler.

Network Reliability

IP security cameras are not dependent on Wi-Fi or other office networks as the cable directly links it to the cloud network. It can work both as an independent camera network and be linked to the security systems of the organization. With the right access, senior security managers can rely on the efficiency of the IP camera system via the internet.

Connected Power

Power over ethernet helps us to connect the IP security camera system to protect the properties of an organization. But PoE is not just used for that purpose only. It can also provide power for other devices in the office like lights, IoT devices, and much more. The future of connected power is not far in that case.

title: Keep Your Credit Card Safe When Shopping Online: Here’s How
excerpt: Shopping online with a credit card is generally pretty safe these days, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t risks. content:
Shopping online with a credit card is generally pretty safe these days, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t risks. A credit card gives you the freedom to buy now and pay later, and when used correctly, a credit card is like an interest-free loan. Although many different types of credit cards may come with rewards or special offers, what makes them safer than cash is their ability to offer you protection against fraud.

While a credit card is a great thing, it’s important to remember that fraudsters are always looking for credit card numbers, passwords, or PINs. Stay alert and keep your personal information safe. While you can’t control things like a data breach at your favorite retailer, you can shop smart and make it harder for thieves to access your information and commit credit card fraud. With a little vigilance, maintenance, and additional layers of security, you can protect your credit card information and online purchases.

So, how can you keep your credit card transactions safe from issues? Here are some tips for you.

  • Private device and secure connection
  • Investigate the merchant and the URL
  • Add a layer of security
  • Credit card app’s security features
  • Routine maintenance

Let’s explore some of them in detail.

ALSO, READ Transform Into A Circular Economy With These 5 Steps

Private device and secure connection

Shop in private, away from prying eyes and potentially infuriating public devices. On a shared computer websites can store login information and leave accounts vulnerable to the next user. Even if you log out of a public computer, you can install spyware that records keystrokes and accesses usernames, passwords, credit card numbers, and personal information.

Using your laptop or tablet is safer, but it’s not completely foolproof. Data can still be stolen over public Wi-Fi. Shop online only with your personal device and private Wi-Fi connection. You may also consider subscribing to a virtual private network or VPN that can encrypt your data. It adds a layer of security to both private and public networks.

Add a layer of security

The security services provided by each credit card company can differ from each other. Some come with added security features that you can utilize to play it safely. Here are three such measures that you can utilize.

Third-party digital wallets

Third-party digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay can provide additional protection because they don’t share your credit card information with the merchant. Instead, they provide a one-time virtual account number for each purchase, called “tokenization.”

Virtual credit card numbers

Credit cards can offer virtual account numbers. You can utilize this instead of the card to make payments which are also more secure.

Payment app checkout

Payment can be done through various smartphone applications these days. Here you don’t have to pay using your cards directly. Payment through the apps will reduce exposing your card details directly to the receiver. The app plays the role of an intermediary in such cases.

Routine maintenance

Securing credit card information requires effort and care. You need to mind the following points.

  • Automatically or manually update apps, browsers, firewalls, and antivirus software on devices.
  • Keep contact information up to date on publisher apps and websites so you can be contacted in the event of potential fraud.
  • Use strong passwords and change them regularly on credit card issuers and merchant platforms.
  • Take the time to review your credit card statements to identify unauthorized transactions and dispute fraudulent charges.

In business, mergers and acquisitions are part of the growth and diversification of the company. It can be good, bad, or ugly depending upon the decisions taken and priorities are given. Based on the phases of the deal that a company interprets, mergers and acquisitions can boost growth. What it requires the most is precise planning, vision, and precise timing.

Here are some of the top phases that should be considered in a merger and acquisition deal:

  1. Develop strategies
  2. Identify target
  3. Analyse the value
  4. Negotiation
  5. Closing deal
  6. Integration

Top 6 Key Phases of a Merger and Acquisition Deal to Note

Now, let’s explore the different stages in detail.

Develop Strategies

A merger and acquisition strategy can help set clear expectations for everyone involved. While every deal is unique, every strategy should address what your company hopes to achieve with the deal and how to get there. Consider the following points:

  • Purpose of the transaction
  • Financing the transaction
  • New operating model
  • Companies involved

Identify Target

Your business cannot merge or acquire any other business randomly. You must identify what you need from the deal and find the best targets to suit your requirements. Legal and finance teams should consider the potential of the merger or acquisition and the market value it can bring to the business later. Proper understanding of the target companies is important in this phase.

Analyze The Value

Each merger and acquisition should add value to the business. Ideally, the result should be “one plus one equal to two” or more. Growth is an important value post the merger or acquisition. One can understand the value of the target company from the data related to operations, financials, products, services, customers, and more. Identifying the growth value after the companies merged is also important for the future development of the business.

Negotiation

Negotiations are an important part of any merger and acquisition deal. Nobody is in the business world for loss, profit rules here. Negotiating with proper channels and the right teams can profit both the companies in the deal. The better the negotiations go the better the results the concerned companies can obtain post the merger and acquisition.

Closing Deal

Once the negotiations and due diligence are done, parties can move forward to close the deals. Legal teams must take care of multiple responsibilities like merger filings, amendments, ordering of good standings, or issuing bring-down letters. The joined entities need to file out the tax documents and complete the necessary legal documents related to the merger and acquisition.

Integration

Integration after the merger and acquisition takes time. Both the parties need to come under one roof. Financing of the business activities needs to be settled properly. Integration starts from the top leadership to the bottom employees as their tasks and responsibilities can also change. Legal documentations need to be filed. If there is a company name change, necessary procedures should be completed. All the departments need to be reshuffled as per the requirement.

Business Continuation

Once the merger and acquisition processes are completed business can proceed as usual. There may be some changes in the structure but with some time it can be handled and go as per usual.

content:
As businesses grow, they need to manage their expenses efficiently. One of the ways to do so is through a business credit card. It allows businesses to track expenses, earn rewards, and streamline cash flow. However, like any financial tool, it also comes with its own set of benefits and challenges. In this article, we will explore the top five benefits of business credit cards.

Benefits of Business Credit Cards

Improved Cash Flow

A business credit card can help improve cash flow by providing a revolving line of credit. This means businesses can pay for expenses even if they don’t have the cash on hand, and then pay the balance off over time. This can be particularly helpful for businesses with irregular income or seasonal fluctuations.

Rewards and Perks

Business credit cards often offer rewards and perks that can be valuable to the business. These can include cashback on purchases, points that can be redeemed for travel, and discounts on office supplies. By using the card for everyday expenses, businesses can earn rewards and save money.

Streamlined Expense Tracking

A business credit card can help businesses track their expenses more efficiently. Most cards come with online expense management tools that allow businesses to categorize and track spending in real-time. This can help businesses stay on top of their finances and make better-informed decisions.

Separation of Personal and Business Expenses

Using a business credit card can help separate personal and business expenses, which is important for accounting and tax purposes. By keeping expenses separate, businesses can avoid confusion and ensure accurate reporting.

Improved Credit Score

Using a business credit card responsibly can help improve the business’s credit score. This can be particularly beneficial when seeking financing or credit in the future.

Business credit cards offer a range of benefits and challenges. While they can help improve cash flow, streamline expense tracking, and offer valuable rewards and perks. Also, they can also come with high-interest rates, fees, and the temptation to overspend. It is important for businesses to carefully consider the pros and cons and use the card responsibly. By doing so, businesses can reap the benefits of a business credit card while avoiding potential pitfalls.

content:
Do you know how many people surf the internet on a daily basis? We don’t know that either. But you can be sure that it is in the billions. What if we say that you can attract a portion of this traffic to you? If you are a business organization, customers are unavoidable to you. But how do you attract this many people to you? The answer is simple – internet marketing.

Internet marketing is about reaching out to the right target audience and attracting your business. This step can be achieved with various means like images, social media posts, carousels, videos, interactive quizzes, or anything attractive. Before getting into all of this, you need to understand why internet marketing is important. Here are seven reasons you should know.

  1. Customers are online
  2. Two-way communication
  3. Audience experience
  4. Drive quality traffic
  5. Business visibility
  6. Multitask
  7. Competition

Let us explore some of these important reasons.

ALSO READ: Keep Your Credit Card Safe When Shopping Online: Here’s How

Customers are online

Billions of people go online, and so do your customers – which is why internet marketing is important. Among these are your potential customers and target audience. People look for everything online.

Once you identify your target audience you can market your products and services in front of them. Your investment in marketing can gain you leads that can be converted into investments, sales, and many more. The right marketing strategies can boost your business.

Two-way communication

Internet communication enables you to interact with your potential customers and convert them into actual customers. Traditional advertisements like newspaper ads, TV ads, flyers, posters, etc are pretty much one-sided. You will never know when they will contact you back. Online marketing strategies engage the target audience where they are frequently.

Active communication channels can be established with them. This creates a two-way communication channel that keeps them engaged, notified, and updated 24/7. The various digital marketing channels and resources can ensure that either party can contact the other at any time.

Drive quality traffic

When comparing traditional marketing and modern marketing methods, the biggest difference is the speed of lead generation. Traditional methods are one-sided, it is inefficient because it comes in front of both interested and uninterested people. You receive less response from such an audience. Internet marketing is much more agile in comparison. It gets directly to the right target audience from which you get a proper response at the right time.

Internet marketing helps you gain information like demographics, purchasing capacity, product requirements, service satisfaction, intent to buy, and much more at a click. Converting the target audience into leads and then into customers is easier. Multiple technologies can help you drive quality traffic to your business, enabling you to gain higher ROIs.
